Duḥśalā, daughter of Dhṛtarāshṭra and Gāndharī. § 130 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 67, 2740, 2744 (married to Jayadratha).-§ 181 (Duḥśalotpatti): I, 116, 4527, 4539 (birth of D.).-§ 182 (Dhṛtarāshṭraputranāmak.): I, 117, 4553, 4557 (married to Jayadratha).--§ 522 (Draupadīharaṇap.): III, 271, 15758 (Yudhishṭhira orders to save Jayadratha for the sake of D.).--§ 523 (Jayadrathavimokshaṇap.): III, 272, 15782 (do.).--§ 615 (Gadāyuddhap.): IX, 64, 3617.-§ 619 (Strīvilāpap.): XI, 22, 629, 632.--§ 785 (Anugītāp.): XIV, 78, 2275 (Dhṛtarāshṭrajā, came with her grandson, the son of her son Suratha), 2280, 2294, 2297; 89, 2678 (her little grandson installed as king of the Sindhus).

[Duḥśalotpatti(ḥ)]
(“birth of Duḥśalā”). § 181 (Sambhavap.): That Gāndhārī also had a daughter (Duḥśalā) was due to the circumstance that Vyāsa, when he divided the lump of flesh (knowing that Gāndhārī wished to have a daughter), assigned one part in excess of the hundred to become a daughter (I, 116).
